alignments.note: Negative purpose particle rendered by the clause-introducer *lest*. Rule 59's joining case does not apply: `τις` is a plain indefinite the ASV renders non-negatively as *any*, so under rule 69 the negator keeps its own English word and the indefinite stands separately. The supplied existential copula *there be* is not part of this unit; see the note on `πόρνος`.
Plain indefinite rendered *any*, carrying no negation of its own (rule 69).

Verbless Greek clause; the ASV supplies the existential frame *there be*, which rides with the predicate noun under rules 53 and 63, discontinuously across the intervening *any* under rule 15. Rule 53's subject-pronoun exception is scoped to a pronoun standing as subject, and *any* here is a determiner on this noun rather than a standalone pronoun. Attaching *there be* to `μή` as part of a supplied clause frame remains defensible, but rule 53 refuses to read a supplied copula off English word order, so it is given to the predicate.

Anarthrous substantival adjective expanded with the generic noun *person*; rule 17's generic-noun clause and rule 66's operational test keep the head on the adjective, *person* being the empty completion.
Comparative adverb; no correlative `καί` stands, so rule 82 is not in question.
Relative pronoun with no supplied antecedent or nominal, so rule 77 does not arise.
Expressed preposition realized by *for*. The ASV spreads the phrase over separate words answering to each token, so rule 94's single-word precondition is not met and the ordinary split applies.
Numeral *one*, kept separate from its noun under rule 26.

One Greek noun rendered by the phrase *mess of meat*. Under rules 66 and 91 the head is the word that glosses the lexeme: `βρῶσις` is food/meat, and *mess* with its partitive *of* is the supplied portion word completing the English expression. Heading on *mess* as the phrase's formal English noun is what rule 17 forbids.

The English determiner slot is occupied by the possessive *his own*, which the reflexive `ἑαυτοῦ` licenses, so the article realizes nothing under rule 20. Variant SBLGNT.HEB.12.16.v009 selected r00-base, which covers s015, so a source word is present and available to take the possessive.

Reflexive genitive rendered *his own*; both words belong to this token, *own* being the reflexive force rather than a separate source word. Rule 47's `ἴδιος` is not in play — no such adjective is expressed here.
Head noun standing bare, its determiner having gone to the reflexive under rule 20.

review_notes: All 15 source and 20 target ids are partitioned exactly once.

Main judgment call: placement of the supplied existential *there be*. Given to the predicate noun `πόρνος` under rules 53 and 63; attaching it to `μή` is the competing reading and is named in that unit's note.
`μή` + `τις` are kept as two units rather than joined, because the ASV renders the indefinite non-negatively as *any* (rule 69), not as *nothing*/*no man* (rules 41, 59).
`βρώσεως` heads on *meat* rather than the formal English noun *mess*, per rules 66, 91 and 17.
The article s013 is `unrepresented` under rule 20, the reflexive `ἑαυτοῦ` carrying *his own*; the selected variant covers s015, so the licensing token is present.
